questions.prompt: What is the intent of the Singleton pattern?

options.text: Ensure a class has only one instance and provide a global point of access to it
Create objects by cloning a prototype
Build a complex object step by step
Create families of related products

questions.explanation: Singleton restricts a class to one instance with global access. Cloning = Prototype; step-by-step = Builder; families = Abstract Factory.

questions.prompt: Which are common, valid criticisms of Singleton? Select all that apply.

options.text: It introduces global mutable state
It hides a class's real dependencies
It makes unit testing harder because state leaks between tests
It always makes programs run faster

questions.explanation: Singleton's downsides are global state, hidden dependencies, and testing pain. It has nothing to do with speed.

questions.prompt: Which two things make a class a Singleton? Select all that apply.

options.text: A private constructor
A static accessor that returns the single instance
A clone() method
A fluent build() method

questions.explanation: A private constructor blocks outside instantiation; a static accessor lazily creates and returns the one instance.

questions.prompt: Why is a Singleton class often unnecessary in TypeScript?

options.text: An ES module is evaluated once, so a module-level export is already a single shared instance
TypeScript forbids the `new` keyword
TypeScript objects are automatically global
Classes cannot have static members in TypeScript

questions.explanation: Modules run once and their exports are shared across imports, giving a single instance without the Singleton ceremony.

questions.prompt: Is the classic 'two threads create two instances' thread-safety concern relevant in JavaScript?

options.text: No — JavaScript is single-threaded, so that race doesn't occur (it matters in multi-threaded languages)
Yes — JavaScript runs every function on its own thread
Yes — and it can only be fixed with locks in JavaScript
It is impossible to create a Singleton in JavaScript

questions.explanation: Single-threaded JS avoids that race; the synchronization concern applies to languages like Java, C#, and C++.

questions.prompt: For most application code, what is usually a better alternative to fetching a Singleton?

options.text: Dependency Injection — create one instance and pass it in, keeping dependencies explicit
Copying the object with a shallow clone everywhere
Making every field public and global
Adding more static methods

questions.explanation: Injecting a single instance keeps dependencies visible and lets tests substitute a fake — avoiding Singleton's worst problems.
